title: Agentic Postgres secret requirements
description: Declares which secrets exist, which service consumes each one, and under what numeric ownership it is materialized. It contains identifiers only -- never a value, and never a hash of a value. This file is what makes the secret grant surface reviewable: a service receives exactly the files listed for it here and nothing else, and adding a grant is a visible diff rather than a runtime accident.

secrets.description: Later sessions append to this list. They do not create separate dotenv files.

name.description: Stable local identifier. Not a value and not a path.

provider_key.description: The exact key fetched from the provider. Retrieval is by exact key, one at a time -- never a folder-wide export.

provider_path.description: Provider folder. No wildcard: a wildcard path would fetch secrets nobody declared, which is exactly the bulk-export pattern this contract exists to forbid.

introduced_in_session.description: The renderer emits Compose secret declarations only for secrets active through the requested session, so a Session 3 database credential declared here does not become a Session 2 mount.

value_kind.description: What the provider bootstrap creates (ADR 0055). `random_hex` is 32 bytes from secrets.token_hex, which is what every secret was until Session 5 declared one that is not a password. `rsa_private_pem` is a 2048-bit RSA private key in PKCS#8 PEM from `openssl genpkey`. Required on every secret rather than defaulted, because a default is how a hex string ends up stored under a name that says key -- and every check in this repository would pass, with the failure surfacing several runs later as a JWKS derived from something that is not a key.

consumers.description: A provider secret consumed by two services is materialized as a separate file in each consumer's directory. There is no shared file and no shared directory. A consumer is on the `compose` plane or the `root` plane (ADR 0054); the second names no service and is granted to no container.

redaction.description: Mandatory and currently single-valued. An enum rather than a boolean because partial redaction -- last four characters, a prefix -- is a thing people ask for, and refusing it needs somewhere to say no.

must_refresh_on_start.description: When true, the bounded last-known-good fallback is refused for this secret and a start with a stale generation fails closed.

one_time_initialization.description: When true, this secret is consumed only while initializing empty state, and writing a new generation of it changes nothing that already exists. `postgres_init_superuser_password` is the case it was added for: the image entrypoint reads it only when the data directory is empty, so replacing the file does NOT rotate the superuser password of a cluster that has already initialised. Declaring that here means rotation tooling can refuse to claim a rotation it did not perform, rather than reporting success because a file changed. Required on every secret so that a new one has to state which kind it is. Named without a trailing `secret` token deliberately: the Session 3 plan proposed `one_time_initialization_secret`, which ADR 0008's terminal-token rule rejects as secret-bearing. See D56.

consumer.description: Two planes, discriminated by a required `plane` (ADR 0054). Separate definitions rather than one loosened definition, so that `uid: 0` stays refused where a container has to read the file and stays required where only root may.

service.description: A real Compose service, or a service a later session declares. Cross-checked against the Compose model by tests/contract/test_secret_contract.py.

target_file.description: A simple basename. The pattern admits no '/' and no '..', so a target filename can never escape its generation directory -- which is the whole reason the filename is not taken from the project manifest.

mode.description: Read-only to the owner. Compose's own file-backed secret uid/gid/mode fields are deliberately not relied upon; the host sets ownership before Compose ever sees the file.

rootConsumer.description: A value no container may hold (ADR 0054): the bootstrap issuer's signing key, and the documentation credential the edge turns into a hash. It names no service, is materialized into `_root/` -- a directory name no Compose service can have, because the service pattern admits no underscore -- and is granted to nothing. `service` is absent rather than null: a null service is a field somebody can fill in.

uid.description: Root, and required to be. The compose plane refuses root ownership because a container that drops privileges could not read the file; this plane requires it, because a file any other uid can read is a file this plane's whole purpose says nobody else may.

format.description: What the materializer writes into this consumer's file (ADR 0056). `raw` is the provider's value byte for byte, which is what every consumer got until Session 5. `pgpass` is `*:*:*:*:{value}` and a newline -- a libpq password file with wildcards in all four match fields. It exists because the PostgREST image is distroless and has no shell to assemble one, and the wildcards are deliberate: naming the host, port, database and role would put four derived identifiers into a materialized secret, which is a second derivation path for names naming.py owns and a file that goes stale when any of them changes. Required on every consumer, so that a service receiving a file in a shape it cannot read is a reviewable line rather than a default.

numericId.description: Fixed and numeric. Zero is excluded: a root-owned secret file mounted into a container that drops privileges is unreadable by the process that needs it, and the failure looks like a provider problem.
